text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired PD#INC_9067 for service=rate-limiter — symptom=high_429_rate, severity=critical. link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC_9067

pagerduty: Incident assigned to maria-s (primary on-call) — please acknowledge.

maria-s: ack. I'm on it. grabbing logs and metrics now.

kevin-g: looking at traces, 429s spike started ~2026-03-14T05:12:30Z right after a config rollout to quota-mapper. Traffic pattern shows many tenants suddenly hitting tiny token buckets.

maria-s: can you paste the deploy id and any suspicious config changes?

kevin-g: deploy id: deploy/quota-mapper@2026-03-14T05:10:12Z sha=abcdef123456. Diff looks like a config change to default quota mapping. snippet:

```
- default_quota: 1000
+ default_quota: 10
```

kevin-g: logs show quota-mapper returning null/misapplied quotas: `applied_quota=null tenant=tenantA request_id=...` repeatedly.

maria-s: ok — mitigation plan: 1) disable the new config rollout 2) rollback quota-mapper to previous stable 3) add temporary bypass for top-tier tenants 4) notify CS for affected customers. Who can run the rollback?

oncall-sre: I'm executing rollback now. running: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/quota-mapper -n prod --to-revision=stable`

incident-bot: Rollback command executed by oncall-sre. Updating PD notes.

oncall-sre: rollout completed successfully; pods restarted and new replicas are running. tailing logs.

maria-s: monitoring metrics — global 429 rate dropped from ~12% to ~3% after rollback but still noisy in US region. Need to identify top affected tenants for targeted bypass.

kevin-g: query results (last 15m): tenantA: 45% of 429s, tenantB: 20%, tenantC: 10%, rest: 25%. Will apply temporary whitelist for tenantA and tenantB via limiter config.

kevin-g: applying whitelist rule: `POST /admin/limiter/rules {"tenant":"tenantA","action":"bypass"}` then same for tenantB.

incident-bot: Admin change logged: limiter bypass rules added for tenantA, tenantB by kevin-g.

maria-s: can someone run a synthetic for tenantA to confirm 200 responses?

kevin-g: running synthetic traffic to tenantA: `python tools/synth_rush.py --tenant tenantA --qps 50 --duration 30s`

kevin-g: synthetic results: 100% 200 OK, latency within 95th pct target.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by maria-s; escalated to platform team as severity-critical.

incident-bot: Auto-escalation triggered to platform-lead due to >30m degraded impact.

cs-lead: CS update: tickets opened for tenantA and tenantB, we've alerted their account teams and asked for patience; they requested ETA for full resolution.

maria-s: current state: rollback complete, bypass rules in place, 429 rate down to ~0.6% cluster-wide. Still watching. Recommended next steps: 1) stabilize for 30m 2) collect config diffs and timeline 3) start RCA/postmortem draft 4) push a fix guard in quota-mapper to prevent zero/default regressions.

anne-p: I'll take the follow-up and postmortem ownership in the next handoff at 06:00 UTC. Please dump the timeline and attach config diffs to the PD incident.

kevin-g: quick note: root cause appears to be a bad default introduced when QUOTA_DEFAULT env was not present — code treated missing env as 0/very small. I'll add a validation fail-fast and a unit test; will ship as a tiny patch after RCA.

maria-s: oncall handoff: anne-p will take over monitoring and RCA. I'm marking this as mitigated and moving to monitoring mode.

oncall-sre: last check at 06:22:10Z: 429 rate 0.6% (baseline ~0.2%). No new deploys to quota-mapper since rollback.

maria-s: leaving detailed notes in PD: actions taken, commands run, top tenants impacted, CS notified.

incident-bot: PD#INC_9067 — Resolved by maria-s. Resolution summary: rollback quota-mapper, apply tenant bypass, verify synthetic traffic, notify customers. Auto-close scheduled in 1h if no regressions. :white_check_mark: 

anne-p: I'll assemble the timeline/ticket and schedule a 1hr RCA tomorrow. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for quota-mapper ownership.

kevin-g: follow-up action items for eng: 1) add env validation and CI guard, 2) add rollout safety check for config changes, 3) improve alerting to surface sudden global quota drops faster.

cs-lead: confirm CS follow-ups: scheduled check-ins with tenantA and tenantB for impact assessment + compensation discussion if needed.

maria-s: thanks everyone — handing to anne-p for postmortem. I'll be available for questions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging — monitoring-only channel will remain open.
